scenes.title: A brief helps someone understand
scenes.narration: An opportunity brief brings your discovery work into one readable summary. It helps a reviewer understand the group, problem, evidence, proposed improvement and next decision. It is not an investor pitch, a validated business case or a reason to hide uncertainty.

scenes.title: Keep one thread through the brief
scenes.visual: Editable group, context and problem cards.
scenes.narration: Use the same group, task and context throughout. If your research changed the focus, say what changed and why. Keep user and possible buyer roles separate. Do not let a broad market description replace the specific experience you are exploring.

scenes.title: Summarise evidence honestly
scenes.visual: Editable known, inferred, planned and unknown labels.
scenes.narration: Choose the most decision-relevant evidence and preserve its source, date, context and limits. Planned research remains planned. Include contradictions and unknowns rather than smoothing them away. A polished paragraph does not make an assumption true, and lesson completion does not verify the research.

scenes.title: Connect alternatives and proposed value
scenes.visual: Editable current approach and provisional benefit cards.
scenes.narration: Describe what people do today, what works and what might be improved. Summarise your opportunity and value proposition as hypotheses. Do not invent competitive superiority, time saved, market size or payment intent. Keep reasons against the opportunity visible.

scenes.title: Show feasibility and the next decision
scenes.visual: Editable constraint, next check and review cards.
scenes.narration: Summarise founder fit, resources and critical constraints. Explain the provisional action and a bounded next check with permission, timing and a signal that could change your mind. A high rating cannot override a missing permission or another blocking constraint.

scenes.title: Create and review the brief
scenes.narration: Create your Opportunity Brief from eight concise sections. Review earlier worksheets manually; the prototype does not merge them for you. Download the brief and check consistency and evidence labels. Next you will use it for the Discover checkpoint: go to further testing, refine or pause.

sections.label: 02 / LEARN
sections.heading: Make the opportunity understandable and reviewable.

children: is a concise summary of your discovery work and proposed next learning step. Aim for a one-page editorial summary, with source references and detailed notes available separately. The worksheet does not enforce page length.

Use one specific group, task and context across the problem, evidence and proposed value. Explain changes in focus rather than silently mixing groups. Preserve user, beneficiary and possible buyer roles.
Problem, desired outcome and why it may matter.
Decision-relevant evidence with source/status and limits.
Founder fit, resources and critical constraints.
Provisional action, next check and review signal.

“We are exploring registration information for first-time visitors. The difficulty is still a hypothesis; observation permission is pending. Staff help may already be sufficient. Our next step is a permitted check of the current process.” This is honest even without completed research.

Do not turn planned research into findings, ratings into proof, or a polished draft into validation. Avoid unsupported market size, traction, quotes, benefit metrics or willingness-to-pay claims. Include conflicting evidence.
Earlier drafts save separately. No source is merged or verified automatically.

Try four scripted guidance modes. The preview reads your current worksheet locally; it does not send information anywhere.

replies.teach: A brief synthesises group, problem, evidence, alternatives, provisional value, unknowns, fit and next decision without hiding limits.
replies.guide: Review earlier worksheets manually. Keep the same group/context, source/status labels, contradictions and critical constraints. Shorten wording without changing evidence status.
replies.review: Opportunity Brief check: {missing} required fields still empty. This scripted check counts fields only; it cannot verify sources, consistency, business claims or demand.
replies.challenge: Did a plan become a finding? Did the group change silently? What source contradicts the story? Does the proposed next action respect constraints?
